resources.string: Magen locks the apps you choose, blocks new installs and protects parts of Settings. It reads on-screen text only to recognise which app or Settings page is open. Nothing leaves your device.
Device admin makes removing Magen require extra steps. Magen does not read or erase your data.
Disabling Magen\'s device-admin permission weakens protection. To remove Magen, use “Approve uninstall” inside the app.
App locking, install blocking and removal protection, all in one place.

If Accessibility cannot be enabled, try turning it on in Accessibility settings. When Android says the setting is restricted, dismiss the warning. Then open Settings > Apps > Magen, tap ⋮ and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Return to Accessibility settings and enable Magen. If ⋮ is missing, try opening App info by long-pressing the Magen icon. Availability depends on Android version and how the app was installed.

Requires a computer, USB debugging, and removing accounts during setup. You can add them back afterward.
Strong mode makes Magen the Device Owner, so Android itself enforces the rules. It is done once from a computer and takes about five minutes.

On the phone, open Settings > About phone and find Build number (sometimes under Software information). Tap it seven times to enable Developer options. Return to Settings > System > Developer options and turn on USB debugging. Menu names vary by manufacturer.

Device Owner setup generally requires that no accounts are signed in. Open Settings > Passwords & accounts (or Accounts) and temporarily remove every account, including Google. If there are additional users or a work profile, remove those as needed. You can add accounts back after setup.

On the computer, download Android SDK Platform-Tools from developer.android.com/tools/releases/platform-tools and extract the archive. Open a command window in the extracted folder. Connect the phone with a USB cable and keep its screen unlocked.

In the command window, run adb devices and press Enter. Approve the USB debugging prompt on the phone if it appears. The device should be listed with status device. If it says unauthorized, approve the prompt and try again.
Copy the command shown here, paste it into the computer\'s command window, and press Enter. If it succeeds, the response will include Success.
Open Magen and check that Strong mode is active. You can now add the accounts you removed. To remove Magen later, use “Approve uninstall” in the More tab.

Device Owner setup fails: check that all accounts and additional users were temporarily removed, then try again.
Computer does not detect the phone: try another USB cable, approve the prompt, and run adb devices again.
Unauthorized: revoke USB debugging authorizations in Developer options, reconnect, and approve the prompt.
Xiaomi or Redmi: you may also need to enable “USB debugging (Security settings)”.

Important: keep your master code somewhere safe. Device Owner changes the device\'s management privileges. Before proceeding, make sure you understand the steps and have a way to recover access to your phone.
Magen needs these to work. Android does not let apps switch them on silently, so each button opens the matching Settings screen.
How to find a Settings page to block

1. Open Settings and search for the option you want to block. 2. Open the result and note the title at the top of the page. 3. Return to Magen > Protection > Block any other page. 4. Enter the title exactly as shown and tap Add. You can also paste a full path, such as Network & internet > Internet; Magen uses the final page name. 5. Try opening the page again to test the block. If it still opens, try another title shown on that screen. Names vary by device maker and language. Strong mode can enforce only restrictions Android supports at system level.

This phone\'s firmware is missing the telephony provider that Android must clean up before it releases Device Owner. From a computer, try: adb shell pm enable --user 0 com.android.providers.telephony (check with: adb shell pm list packages telephony), then retry. If the package does not exist on this phone, only a factory reset removes Device Owner.
The normal removal does not work on this phone (its firmware lacks a component Android needs). Use the Root removal or hand ownership to Magen Keeper.

Warning: this is NOT Android\'s official removal method and it may not work on every device or Android version. Magen will clear its restrictions, then use Root to move the file where Android stores the Device Owner registration (/data/system/device_owner_2.xml) to a backup file next to it. You must then reboot. Your data is not erased. If the phone ends up in an unexpected state, restoring the backup file or a factory reset may be needed. Use it only if the normal button fails and your phone is rooted. Root permission will be requested.
The Device Owner registration file was moved to a backup. Reboot to finish. Afterwards Magen runs in Regular protection; you can check from a computer with: adb shell su -c \"dpm list-owners\".
Transfer Device Owner to Magen Keeper?

Magen clears its restrictions and hands Device Owner to the small Magen Keeper app, using Android\'s official transfer. Magen is then no longer the owner and can be uninstalled. Later, a reinstalled Magen can take ownership back from Keeper (More, Strong mode). Needs Android 9 or newer and Magen Keeper installed.
Magen Keeper is not installed. Install the Magen Keeper app first, then try again.
Device Owner was handed to Magen Keeper. Magen is now in Regular protection.
Take Device Owner from Magen Keeper
Magen is the Device Owner again.
Magen Keeper did not hand over Device Owner.

If removing Device Owner from Magen fails on your phone, install the small Magen Keeper app and use \"Transfer to Magen Keeper\" in More. Magen then stops being the owner and can be uninstalled. After installing Magen again, the Strong mode card shows \"Take Device Owner from Magen Keeper\", with no adb needed. Keeper can also hand ownership to any other app that supports it. Needs Android 9 or newer.
Magen Keeper is installed but its device-admin is not enabled. Open Magen Keeper, tap \"Enable device admin\", then try again.
To take Device Owner from Magen Keeper, first enable Magen as a device administrator (the card above).

Which method works on which Android:
• Simple removal: Android 6 and newer (Magen's minimum). Google marked it deprecated in Android 8, no upper limit is documented, but it can fail on some phones.
• Transfer to Magen Keeper: Android 9 (API 28) and newer only. Keeper must be installed and its device admin enabled.
• Root removal: unofficial, depends on the phone.

Android still blocks uninstalling Magen, although Magen is no longer the Device Owner. It is a leftover from an older Strong mode, and only a Device Owner can clear it. One-time fix: run the command below from a computer (it may require removing accounts first). Magen then clears the block by itself within seconds. After that, remove Device Owner again if needed and uninstall. Magen does not edit system files for this.
